execution_policy: Toolchains are represented as NSQ contracts. A host binary is consulted only on explicit invocation, never retained as a resident runtime.

semantic_intent.description: Instantiate language meaning as an NSQ semantic contract before optional compiler or assembler invocation. Foreign spellings are ingress and egress projections, not the inner-system authority.

languages.output_contract: Cargo package, Rust binary, library, or test artifact invoked only on demand
notes: The retired 1.97 beta channel resolves to the matching archived Rust 1.97.0 release for reproducible installation.
Rust source is semantically represented in NSQ before an optional rustc or cargo process is invoked.

languages.output_contract: Native object, archive, or executable generated on demand through the approved native toolchain
notes: C is a first-class NSQ symbolic contract rather than an untracked exterior compiler dependency.
The actual compiler path is probed at bootstrap and must be supplied by the native Tower environment on device.

languages.resolved_toolchain: python3 interpreter and standard-library boundary codec
languages.output_contract: Python source, package, test artifact, or explicit interpreter invocation generated and invoked only on demand
notes: Python 3 is a first-class NSQ alphabetic contract; Python spelling is accepted only as an ingress or egress boundary projection.
The interpreter is consulted only for an explicitly requested boundary action and cannot become a resident Braxon runtime.
Target-side execution requires the declared Tower native CPython boundary tool to be present and verified during device bootstrap.

languages.resolved_toolchain: clang integrated assembler, llvm-mc, llvm-objcopy, llvm-objdump
languages.output_contract: Architecture-specific native object or ELF artifact generated only after explicit routing
notes: Assembly is bound to the NSQ stamp dialect and is not silently delegated outside the Reflexor contract.
AArch64 is a device boundary target only; compilation authority stays in the native Tower toolchain contract.
